source_text: Quod autem verba apostolica, ubi dicit: Scio quia non habitat in me, hoc est in carne mea, bonum [n180] ; et cetera usque ad illud, ubi ait: Miser ego homo, quis me liberabit de corpore mortis huius? [n181] "Me - affirmas - aliter intellegere, quam totum ipsum capitulum debet intellegi": nesciens mihi plurimum tribuis. … Contra quos motus, prius utique debellandos ne dominentur, et postea sanandos ut penitus exstinguantur, etiam ipse gloriosa certamina sanctos exercere confessus es
pass_a_gloss: But that the apostolic words, where he says: I know that there does not dwell in me, that is in my flesh, good; and the rest up to that where he says: Wretched man I, who will free me from the body of this death? 'I, you affirm, understand otherwise than the whole chapter itself ought to be understood': unknowing, you attribute very much to me. Against which movements, first certainly to be warred down lest they dominate, and afterwards to be healed so that they be thoroughly extinguished, you yourself also confessed that the saints exercise glorious contests.
pass_b_english: Augustine reports, speaking to Julian: “As for the Apostle’s words where he says, ‘I know that good does not dwell in me, that is, in my flesh,’ and the rest up to where he says, ‘Wretched man that I am, who will free me from the body of this death?’ (Romans 7:18–24): you affirm ‘that I understand them otherwise than that whole passage ought to be understood.’ Without knowing it, you credit me with a great deal.”

“Against these movements, which must first be fought down so that they do not rule, and afterward healed so that they are wholly put out, you yourself also admitted that the saints wage glorious struggles.”

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

choices.choice: The movements are the carnales concupiscentiae of the preceding sentence, which is not translated here; stated in the translator note rather than supplied in brackets in the reading text.

2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-d): the old English summarised Augustine's report ('Augustine reports that Julian ...') instead of translating it. Now a translation of the Latin clause(s) that carry Julian's words or Augustine's report of them, with Augustine named as speaker where the words are his; nothing added that the Latin does not say. Omitted stretches inside a paragraph are marked with an ellipsis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

bible_refs.note: Inline in Pass B; verse text checked against the quoted words.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here. This row translates Augustine's report addressed to Julian, with Augustine named as speaker; Julian's words are the quoted parts.
